correctness.rationale: For all n>=2, lambda>0, tau>=0, the Gaussian posterior weights are (K+tau 11^T)^{-1}m with SPD covariance. The explicit inverse K^{-1} of the exponential Toeplitz correlation is tridiagonal and gives K^{-1}m=u(1,2,...,2,1) and K^{-1}1=(1,1-r,...,1-r,1)/(1+r). Sherman–Morrison gives all displayed weights. Their only potentially negative factor is 1-(n-2)tau, proving the sharp frontier. The signed weak limit is exact from endpoint limits and interior Riemann sums; the independent-noise positivity comparison follows from inverse positivity of a diagonally dominant M-matrix. Verified computations are 660 exact rational cases and 210 independent numerical solves in the embedded verifier; these support algebra but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural numerical-integration stability question under shared calibration uncertainty. The full n and lambda-uniform positivity classification is not a merely rebranded known independent-noise result: an arbitrarily small fixed common bias eventually forces negative endpoint weights, while any finite independent noise preserves positivity. The exact negative mass bounds worst negative output on bounded nonnegative observations. The nonvanishing negative endpoint atoms in the dense-grid limit demonstrate a genuine structural obstruction with direct relevance to correlated sensing and kernel integration, rather than an arbitrary isolated computation.
